description:
FILED s521 (Fable, 2026-10-18 18:5x) beside #3516, from the same probe (scratchpad rv/globstr3.pl): identical on the ed8a4504 base and on main, so PRE-EXISTING (not s521a's).
    sub via_arg { my $rval = \$_[0]; return "" . $$rval }
    open(my $fh, '<', $0) or die; bless $fh, 'Z';
    print via_arg($$fh), "\n";     # perl *main::$fh      PCL Z=GLOB(0x...)
perl names an anonymous lexical handle's glob `*main::$fh` (the variable's name); PCL's glob value for an `open my $fh` handle has no glob name, so its stringification falls through to the blessed-reference form.  Low: Data::Dump of a blessed lexical filehandle is the only known consumer (it would print `bless(\Z=GLOB(...), "Z")` instead of `bless(\*main::$fh, "Z")`).  FIX SHAPE: when #3516 is fixed, the glob VALUE's string for a nameless lexical handle should be `*main::$NAME` (perl's `$fh`-named glob) -- the emitter knows the variable name at the `open my $fh` site; record it on the handle's glob as perl does.  Probe `"" . *$fh` directly too.  A filler.


=== DONE (s521e, 2026-10-19, commit 3f98ba9d) ===
FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): %p-fh-install-arg -- THE handle argument of every opener -- notes a SCALAR-VARIABLE target's box with the variable's source name (case inversion undone, a compiler renaming suffix dropped); the two installers (%p-install-fh's box arm, opendir's box arm) give the installed handle (current package . name); %p-stream-glob copies it onto the glob as a DISPLAY name (*p-glob-display-names*) -- the glob's internal name stays unique because %p-resolve-fh finds a glob's handle by NAME; the three readers (glob stringification, *g{NAME}, *g{PACKAGE}) ask %p-glob-perl-name / %p-glob-perl-package.  Two more shapes in the same place: `$$fh` on a lexical handle returned the handle OBJECT (stringified as a blessed GLOB(0x..)) -- perl's $$fh IS the glob, now %p-stream-glob; and FABLE'S r6: `*$dh` on a dirhandle stringified PCL's (index . entries) record into the glob NAME (`*main::0 . .. .claude ...`) -- p-dynamic-typeglob now gives a dirhandle its glob (%p-dirhandle-record-p), registered in *p-dirhandles*, so `readdir *$dh` reads (it read nothing on the base too).
PROBES = perl 5.40.3: Fable's e5 r1-r6 (`*main::$fh` x3, `$fh main`, IO::File `*Symbol::GEN0` unchanged, `*main::$dh`); scratch/s521e/pr/e6.pl: a closure-captured (renamed) lexical `*main::$cap`, `package Foo` `*Foo::$q`, socket `*main::$s`, pipe `*main::$pw`, `our $g` `*main::$g`, `print {$$out}` / `print {*$out}` still write, `fileno($$q)`, readdir *$dh.
BAR: guard Pl/t/bless-referent-01.t t15 (inverse on base-aff112d7: `Z=GLOB(0x5) *pcl-anonio::__anonio__1 __anonio__1 pcl-anonio ... *main::0 . .. .claude ...`); targeted: bareword-fh-slot-01 diamond-01 handle-place-01 opendir-01 tie-01 tiehandle-01 glob-slot-operand-01 transpile-test-10 pass; ir-spec row.  RESIDUE filed #3590 (an ELEMENT target: perl `*main::$h{...}`).
subject: PRE-EXISTING: a blessed OPEN handle's glob value (`open my $fh, ...; bless $fh, 'Z'`) passed through @_ stringifies as `Z=GLOB` where perl prints `*main::$fh` -- the lexical-handle glob has no name string in PCL (its to-string falls to the reference form); LOW
